findings.title: A permanently incomplete exploration branch is durably reused but never receives a terminal rejected-root state
reproduction: Create a private synthetic32-world exploration journal with valid identity/profile/layout fields; one branch has complete=false,y=null,W=null and a permanent physical-cap reason.
The new resume validator accepts these correctly typed incomplete rows. All32 keys are present, so the actual selector has zero pending tasks.

The actual exploration-means block throws exploration branch incomplete: root rejected on both simulated exec2 and exec3; no catch creates a terminal root report. The fixed parent queue therefore keeps selecting this root.
findings.impact: A valid finite-cap outcome can permanently stop the ordered pilot prefix. Repeated ordinal-only resumes cannot repair it because the same incomplete evidence is skipped and no terminal rejection lets the queue advance. Deadline incompletes also need a different treatment from permanent physical caps rather than becoming irreversible completed cache entries.
findings.requestedFix: Classify incomplete outcomes. Preserve deadline evidence without marking a world completed so only the same fixed world may resume. When the fixed exploration contains a permanent cap, write a source/spec/world/journal-bound terminal rejection with no label and fullyAdjudicated=false, and let the parent validate it before advancing the fixed queue. Do not replace worlds/sources or convert incompleteness to loss.

reproduction: Keep the original stats-result.json unparseable after a legitimate interrupted write. Exec2 recomputes the same fixed input into stats-recompute-exec-2-<time>.json and appends statistics:validated, then is interrupted before root-report.json.

findings.impact: An interruption at a valid checkpoint prevents every subsequent resume even though all fixed branch data and statistics are complete. The new digest correctly rejects changed identities, but recovery chooses a new identity each time.
findings.requestedFix: Use a stable recovery identity or reuse the already validated proof statsPath after checking root/input/source/pair/output digests and fresh fixed-input recomputation. Preserve the malformed original and recovery receipt; retain idempotent proof identity across repeated interruptions without producing new worlds.
